english.title: Make untrue statement in answer required by law to a question put by an officer of HMRC
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowingly or recklessly made a statement for a purpose of an assigned matter which was untrue in a material particular, namely **(..SPECIFY UNTRUE DETAILS..), in answer to a question by **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), an officer of His Majesty's Revenue and Customs, which you were required by or under an enactment, namely **(..SPECIFY ENACTMENT..) to answer
english.legislation: Contrary to section 167(1)(b) and (2) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

english.notes:
(i) Any goods in relation to which the statement was made shall be liable to forfeiture (section 167(1)).
(ii) Where by reason of a statement the full amount of any duty payable is not paid or any overpayment is made in respect of any drawback, allowance, rebate or repayment of duty, the amount of the duty unpaid or of the overpayment shall be recoverable as a debt due to the Crown or may be summarily recovered as a civil debt (section 167(4)).
(iii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding £20.000.

INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Proceedings for an indictable offence shall not be commenced after the end of the period of 20 years beginning with the day on which the offence was committed (section 146A(2) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979).
